section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study (Study 1) conducted with 309 Portuguese women from the general population. The study examined a path model exploring how social safeness and connectedness, self-reassurance strategies, and body-image appreciation relate to eating psychopathology symptoms while controlling for BMI. Key findings indicate that social safeness is linked to self-reassurance capacity, which in turn is associated with positive body appreciation and lower eating psychopathology severity, with the model explaining 22-51% of variance across different eating concern dimensions.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents the Discussion of a single study conducted with 309 Portuguese women from the general population. The study tested a path model examining how social safeness and self-reassurance mediate the relationship between body appreciation and eating psychopathology symptoms (restraint, eating concern, weight concern, and shape concern), while controlling for BMI. The model explained 22-51% of variance across the outcome variables, with findings suggesting that adaptive emotion regulation processes (self-reassurance and positive body image) are protective mechanisms against disordered eating.
